ios.desc:
CryDecoder: The Advanced AI Cry Analyzer

Stop the 3 AM guessing game. CryDecoder is a state-of-the-art AI cry analyzer designed to help parents instantly understand why their baby is crying.

Using advanced audio signal processing and the latest AI reasoning, CryDecoder acts as your personal baby cry translator, turning confusing sounds into clear, actionable insights. Whether it's hunger, sleepiness, or a diaper change, get the answers you need in seconds.

HOW IT WORKS:

Record: Capture 5-10 seconds of your baby’s cry.

Analyze: Our AI cry analyzer processes the acoustic patterns.

Understand: Receive a confidence-weighted result (Hungry, Tired, Gassy, or Fussy).

CORE FEATURES: 
• Precision AI Cry Analyzer: Deciphers infant sounds with high accuracy. 
• Smart Baby Translator: Get real-time translations of your baby's needs. 
• Contextual Reasoning: Our AI considers feeding and sleep times for better results. 
• Personalized Learning: The more you use it, the more it learns your baby’s unique voice. 
• Soothing Guidance: Get expert-backed tips to calm your baby faster. 
• Secure & Private: Your baby's data is encrypted and never shared.

WHY PARENTS TRUST CRYDECODER: 
• End the Guesswork: No more wondering if they are hungry or just tired. 
• Faster Soothing: Calmer babies mean better sleep for the whole family. 
• Simple Design: One-tap analysis built for sleep-deprived parents. 
• Smart Monitor Helper: Complements your existing baby monitor routine.

Disclaimer: CryDecoder is a supportive parenting tool and is not a medical device. Always consult with a pediatrician for health concerns.

Download CryDecoder today and use the power of AI to analyze your baby’s cry with confidence.

show_hn.title: Show HN: CryDecoder – On-device ML for classifying baby cries (Swift, Core ML)

quotes.text:
Hi HN,
I’m the developer behind CryDecoder. I built this after too many nights at 3am staring at a crying infant, completely exhausted, trying to guess whether it was hunger, gas, or just general fussiness.

I realized I was essentially running a mental decision tree on very little sleep, so I decided to see if I could automate some of that signal processing.

What it does:
CryDecoder analyzes short audio clips of a baby’s cry and classifies them into categories like hunger, discomfort/gas, tiredness, or general fussiness.

How it works:
• Tech: On-device audio feature extraction paired with a lightweight ML model trained on labeled cry patterns.
• Performance: Inference runs locally on the phone, which keeps latency low and avoids sending audio off-device. Results come back quickly enough to feel near real-time.
• Philosophy: This isn’t meant to replace parental judgment. It’s intended as an extra data point — a sanity check when you’re tired and not sure what to try next.

The business side:
The app currently uses a paid model with a preview. I’m an engineer first and still iterating on pricing and paywall placement.

I’d appreciate feedback on: 
1. The technical approach and responsiveness
2. Whether the paywall timing feels reasonable for a utility like this

Thanks for taking a look.
